item.evidence: App.js:24 creates one module-level QueryClient; :41 keeps its provider outside ClerkAuthProvider. lib/api.js:35 uses the supplied key without user identity. Home.jsx:13 uses ['home'], Profile.jsx:13-15 uses ['me'], ['stats'], ['trips']. AppShell.jsx:41,52 delegates sign-out to UserButton; no cache clearing occurs.
item.expected: R-001: "lands signed in on Inicio with their own empty profile"; request: "Cada usuario tendrá sus propios viajes, países, ciudades, fotografías, estadísticas y logros"; checklist, Auth, sessions and access control: "Sign-out clears the user's caches/client state".
item.observed: Auth, sessions and access control: source predicts that account B signing in in the same SPA within the cache retention period immediately receives A's cached private data while B's refetch runs. If that refetch fails, A's data remains available. This discloses travel history, profile and potentially gallery data on shared browsers, and contradicts the empty-new-account outcome; reload clears the in-memory cache but cannot undo disclosure.
reproduction_steps: Sign in as A and open Inicio and Mi perfil with saved private trips.
Use Mi cuenta to sign out without reloading the browser.
Register or sign in as B in the same tab and open Inicio/Mi perfil; inspect the cached data before refetch completion or when the refetch fails.
item.surface: Sign-out and sign-in; Inicio, Mi perfil, Mi Mundo and detail pages
item.title: A second account sees the previous traveler's private dashboard — account-independent query cache survives sign-out

item.evidence: server.py:659 serve_file takes only photo_id, :660 looks up {'id': photo_id, 'is_deleted': False}, :663-665 returns bytes with 'Cache-Control': 'public, max-age=86400'. There is no viewer, owner, profile visibility or share grant check. file_url at :87-88 exposes this same stable URL everywhere.
item.expected: request: "Cada usuario podrá decidir qué información quiere compartir", "Perfil privado" and "Mostrar u ocultar fotografías"; checklist, Auth, sessions and access control: "Follow ... expired grants ... through every supported access path". Private media should be owner-authorized or covered by an explicit current share grant.
item.observed: Auth, sessions and access control: anyone who retains a photo URL from a previously public profile can continue fetching the original after the owner makes the profile private or hides photographs. The private-by-default owner's file also needs no authentication if its URL is forwarded. URLs are UUIDs, so enumeration is not established; disclosure to existing link holders and public caching are established by source, not runtime execution. Owners have no safe privacy revocation short of deleting the photo.
reproduction_steps: Publish a profile with a gallery photograph and retain the photograph's /api/files URL in another browser.
As owner, disable Mostrar fotografías and make the profile private.
As a signed-out visitor, open the retained file URL; the handler still returns the bytes.
item.surface: GET /api/files/{photo_id}; profile privacy switches
item.title: Private travel photos remain accessible to signed-out link holders — file delivery has no privacy authorization

item.evidence: server.py:727-728 includes every public trip via enrich_trip(light=True), irrespective of show_cities/show_photos. enrich_trip :346 uses {**t}, preserving share_token, and :348 includes city names and ids. public_trip :761 checks only share_token, :765 enriches all cities, :769 returns gallery photos without consulting profile privacy. Public city records inside full trip enrichment also retain their share_token.
item.expected: request: "Mostrar u ocultar ciudades", "Mostrar u ocultar fotografías" and "Compartir viajes individualmente"; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "Responses exclude secrets ... tokens and other users' data". A public listing must not distribute unrestricted share credentials or bypass visibility choices.
item.observed: Auth, sessions and access control: source predicts that an owner who has shared a trip, exposes that trip on a public profile, and disables cities/photos still discloses city names in the public-profile response plus the bearer token that opens the full gallery. The visitor need not be an authorized recipient of the owner's separately generated share link. Turning the profile private does not revoke the leaked trip token. This leaks travel locations and private photographs; it is not merely a hidden UI section.

Make the profile public but disable Mostrar ciudades and Mostrar fotografías.
Read its public profile response: trips still includes city names and the share token.
Open /compartir/viaje/<returned token> signed out; the city list and photographs are served.
item.surface: GET /api/public/users/{username}; /compartir/viaje/:token
item.title: Public-profile visitors can retrieve hidden cities and photos — trip serialization leaks unrestricted share tokens

item.evidence: storage.py:15 posts initialization using only os.environ.get('EMERGENT_LLM_KEY'); :16 requires success and :17 requires storage_key. backend/.env configures database, Clerk and demo settings but has no storage authentication setting; no other app configuration supplies this value. server.py:580 calls storage.put_object for every upload, and :888-891 logs startup initialization errors without providing a fallback.
item.expected: request: "Las fotografías deben poder subirse y visualizarse" and "Almacenamiento de imágenes: almacenamiento externo preparado para producción"; checklist, Third-party integrations: "When every configuration source ... leaves a required provider value empty ... file the blocked feature".
item.observed: Third-party integrations: in the supplied configuration, unless deployment injects the absent storage credential at runtime, initialization sends a null authentication value and cannot obtain the required authenticated storage key. Every real photo/avatar/cover upload depends on that initialization; the UI reports failure and the required photo task cannot complete. This is a configuration-dependent source prediction, not an observed provider response. Supplying the runtime credential is the override that would change this conclusion.
reproduction_steps: Deploy using the repository's supplied backend configuration without injecting a storage credential.
Sign in and open a city.
Choose Subir fotografías and select a valid JPEG; initialization has no authentication value and the upload cannot complete.
item.surface: Subir fotografías; Añadir ciudad/país with photos; profile avatar and trip cover
item.title: Photo uploads cannot initialize with the supplied configuration — storage authentication is missing

item.evidence: AddCityDialog.jsx:41 POSTs city before :42 uploads files; failure goes to :47 with no refresh or retained city id. AddCountryDialog.jsx:33 creates visited country before :35 uploads photo; catch :42 leaves creation mode. server.py:275-276 rejects an already recorded country.
item.expected: checklist, UI state, navigation and interaction: "Read ... every durable/external effect and visible result together" and "a failed save preserving input"; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "Multi-document operations leave no half-written state on failure". A retry must continue the same saved intent or clearly expose the partial result.
item.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: if upload fails (provider outage, oversized file, interrupted request), the earlier entity is already durable but the dialog reports failure and remains open without refreshing lists. Retrying Guardar ciudad or Crear viaje creates another entity, and retrying a country always returns 'Ya tienes este país registrado' instead of finishing its photo. Users must close, find the partially saved item and repair it manually, with duplicate visits corrupting their counts. Source-predicted failure sequence; no runtime calls made.
reproduction_steps: Create a city with a photograph larger than 25 MiB (or during a storage outage).
Press Guardar ciudad and, if prompted, Solo la ciudad.
After the error, press Guardar ciudad again.
Close the dialog and reload Mis ciudades: the city was created on both attempts. Repeat the country flow to see the duplicate-country rejection instead.
item.surface: Añadir ciudad; Nuevo viaje with cover; Añadir país visitado with photo
item.title: A failed photo upload leaves saved cities/trips/countries behind and retries create duplicates or get stuck — creation commits before attachment work

item.evidence: server.py:571-574 accepts any declared image/* or video/*; :575 reads unvalidated bytes; :580 stores them unchanged. serve_file :664 serves original bytes with rec['content_type'], :665 supplies only a public cache header, with no attachment disposition, sandbox or content security policy.
item.expected: checklist, Files, media and generated artifacts: "Trace upload ... validation on the server, type/size limits"; checklist, Auth, sessions and access control: "untrusted HTML rendering". A photo uploader must not allow another user to execute untrusted active documents as trusted app-origin content.
item.observed: Auth, sessions and access control: an authenticated uploader can store a script-capable SVG labeled image/svg+xml and forward its file URL. When another traveler directly opens that URL as a document, the server serves active content on the API origin rather than a safe decoded image. This creates a stored-script execution path in the trusted application origin; access to credentials and user data depends on the browser's session state and same-origin deployment, but execution of attacker-supplied content in that origin follows from the response. No attack payload or runtime execution is asserted.
reproduction_steps: As a signed-in user, upload a script-capable SVG as an image through the supported upload API.
Obtain its returned file URL.
Have another signed-in traveler open the file URL directly in the same-origin deployment; the response is an active SVG document, not sanitized or sandboxed media.
item.surface: POST /api/photos; GET /api/files/{photo_id}
item.title: Uploaded active SVG content can run on the application's backend origin — media validation trusts the supplied MIME type

item.evidence: server.py:618 defaults limit to 200; :626 calls to_list(limit) and returns no total, offset or cursor. item.surface: City Galería; trip Galería del viaje; GET /api/photos

The endpoint reports success and the UI discards the selection, giving no warning that one selected file was ignored; city creation reports complete success. The owner can unintentionally leave photos publicly accessible on A after moving the city into a private B. This persistent cross-view/share mismatch follows from source; repair requires individually re-uploading/removing media rather than the offered move action.
reproduction_steps: Create trips A and B, add a city and photographs under A, and share A.
Open the city → Editar → Viaje, select B and Guardar cambios.
Open B: its photo count includes the city but Galería del viaje does not.
Open A or its shared link: the moved city's photographs still appear.
item.surface: Editar ciudad → Viaje; trip gallery and shared trip gallery
item.title: Moving a city leaves its photographs in the old trip's shared gallery — photo trip references are never reassigned

item.evidence: create_city at server.py:476-479 adds a city's country to its trip's country_codes. update_city :507-508 only checks the trip exists and :515 changes the city; it never updates the destination trip's country_codes. country_detail :305 locates trips solely by that array; TripCard.jsx:20-23 and TripDetail.jsx:49 use enriched countries from it.

Reassignment must apply the same country-membership rule as initial city creation.
item.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: moving a French city into a trip initially containing only Italy does not add France to the trip's countries. Its city list contains France but country flags/card labels omit it and the trip is absent from France's Viajes section. This is a recoverable organization error; manually editing the trip countries is an available but undisclosed repair. Source-predicted, not executed.
reproduction_steps: Create a trip with Italy as its only country.
Create Paris separately and use Editar ciudad → Viaje to assign it to that trip.
Open the trip's card/details and France's country detail: country labels and trip membership remain inconsistent.
item.surface: Editar ciudad → Viaje; trip cards; country Viajes section
item.title: Assigned cities do not add their country to the destination trip — update skips the country synchronization used on creation

item.evidence: stats.py:60 deduplicates cities by (name.strip().lower(), country_code), discarding lat/lng and admin1 stored by CityIn (server.py:419-422). server.py:248 similarly $addToSet's only lowercased names within a country. CitySearch.jsx:41 shows admin1 specifically to distinguish search results.
item.expected: request: "Número de ciudades visitadas", "Las ciudades tendrán sus propias estadísticas independientes" and "Buscador mundial de ciudades"; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "Establish logical record ... identity". Two different municipalities with the same label in one country are distinct cities; repeated visits to the same geographic city are not extra distinct cities.
item.observed: Business logic and calculations: a traveler recording Springfield, Illinois and Springfield, Massachusetts has two different saved locations (different admin1 and coordinates) but receives one visited city in worldwide and country statistics. This also delays city-count achievements. Both remain separately listed, making the count inconsistent. The demonstrated scope is same-named municipalities within a country; user must rename records as a workaround, losing their correct geographic names.
reproduction_steps: Add two worldwide city search results named Springfield in different US states.
Save both with their original names and distinct coordinates.
Open Mis estadísticas and the US badge in Mis países: both count only one distinct city despite the two separate destinations.
item.surface: Mis estadísticas → ciudades; Mis países → city count; city achievements
item.title: Different same-named cities count as one destination — geographic identity is reduced to name and country

item.evidence: stats.py:84 counts one country occurrence per city; :85-86 adds every trip country, including pending trips, to the same Counter. :89-91 labels the winner most_visited_country. Stats.jsx:52-54 displays this as 'País más visitado'.
item.expected: request: "País más visitado"; checklist, Business logic and calculations: "Establish ... eligible records". Inferred meaning: adding cities inside one visit does not create additional visits to that country, and an unvisited pending trip is not a completed visit. Thus one Italy trip covering four cities is one country visit, while two distinct Germany trips are two visits.
item.observed: Business logic and calculations: one completed Italy trip with four cities contributes five Italy occurrences; two completed Germany trips with one city each contribute four Germany occurrences. The app calls Italy the most visited country although Germany was visited twice versus Italy once. Adding untraveled pending trips can change the result too. This materially misstates a requested personal metric but does not destroy the history; source prediction, not measured behavior.
reproduction_steps: Record one completed Italy trip with four city records.
Record two completed Germany trips, each with one city.
Open Mis estadísticas → País más visitado: Italy wins the implemented counter despite fewer actual country visits.
item.surface: Mis estadísticas → País más visitado
item.title: The most-visited-country tile rewards cities and planned trips rather than actual visits — unrelated record types are summed

item.evidence: stats.py:50 loads all trips with no status/time condition; :110 sums trip_days(t) over every trip. trip_days :20-21 computes the full inclusive date span. Stats.jsx:33 renders the result as 'días viajando'. TripDialog.jsx:10 defaults new trips to pendiente.
item.expected: request: "Días viajando" shown automatically in "Mis estadísticas"; checklist, Business logic and calculations: "Establish ... eligible records ... overlapping/excluded groups". A future pending trip has contributed zero days actually spent traveling; for a newly registered user with only a future 10-day plan, the traveled-day total must remain zero.
item.observed: Business logic and calculations: a user who has never traveled but creates a future pending 10-day trip is immediately credited with 10 días viajando. In-progress trips similarly credit their entire future duration. The tile overstates completed travel rather than distinguishing planned days, misleading the user's requested history statistics; this is recoverable by deleting the plan, which is not a correct way to maintain a travel organizer.
reproduction_steps: On an empty account create a pending trip for January 1–10 of a future year.
Open Mis estadísticas without changing status or traveling.
The days tile is 10 rather than zero.
item.surface: Mis estadísticas → días viajando
item.title: Planned future trips count as time already spent traveling — days statistic sums every full trip interval

item.evidence: server.py:329 permits country_codes=None in TripUpdate; clean_trip :362 skips normalization for None; update_trip :392-395 persists it before enrich_trip :347 iterates t.get('country_codes', []). That iteration fails for stored null. CityUpdate :433 permits name=None; :506-515 persists it; stats.py:60 then calls c['name'].strip(). The supplied OpenAPI explicitly advertises these null values.
item.expected: checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "Compare request/response contracts ... omitted/empty/null values" and "partial updates preserve omitted fields"; checklist, code-quality: runtime paths avoid unhandled 5xx. Explicitly accepted null updates must either have safe clearing semantics or be rejected before persistence.
item.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: supported API clients sending country_codes:null receive a 500 after the trip has already been poisoned; subsequent trip/list and applicable home reads fail on the same stored value. Sending name:null for a city persists successfully but breaks /stats and /home for that user. The normal UI cannot open the broken data to repair it in some of these paths, so core dashboard/history access requires a corrective API call or developer help. This is a complete source trace, not an executed request.
reproduction_steps: Using the documented API as an authenticated owner, update an existing trip with country_codes set to null.
Open that trip and Mi perfil; enrichment now iterates null and fails.
Alternatively update a city's name to null, which the documented schema allows, then open Inicio or Mis estadísticas.
item.surface: PUT /api/trips/{trip_id}; PUT /api/cities/{city_id}; Inicio/Mi perfil/Mis estadísticas
item.title: Documented null updates can disable an owner's dashboard and trips — nullable required values are persisted before unsafe reads

item.evidence: CityIn :423-424 and CityUpdate :434-435 use unconstrained strings for dates. create_city :480-484 and update_city :506-515 persist them without ordering checks. AddCityDialog.jsx:36 passes date inputs straight through; :52-55 checks only selected city/country. CityEditDialog.jsx:19-20 likewise has no ordering guard. TripDialog.jsx:28 has a client-only ordering check, but server clean_trip :361-366 does not.
item.expected: request: city ficha must contain "Fecha de visita" and city creation must "Indicar fechas"; checklist, Business logic and calculations: "server validation of ... formats ... ranges". A visit or trip end cannot precede its start; malformed dates must not be stored as valid history.
item.observed: Business logic and calculations: users can save a city with Desde 2026-06-10 and Hasta 2026-06-01 in the normal UI. It is displayed as an impossible reversed stay with no field error. API trip creation/update can bypass the trip dialog check and persist reversed or malformed ranges too; trip_days silently turns a reversed interval into one day. Users have to detect and repair inconsistent history/statistics themselves.
reproduction_steps: Choose Añadir ciudad and select a city.
Set Desde to June 10, 2026 and Hasta to June 1, 2026.
Guardar ciudad accepts the visit and its ficha renders the reversed range.
Through the documented trip API, save the same reversed range; the trip reports one day instead of rejecting it.
item.surface: Añadir ciudad and Editar ciudad date fields; trip/city write APIs
item.title: Impossible visit ranges are saved without errors — city forms and server handlers omit date validation

item.evidence: delete_city :522 deletes the city and :523 marks its photos is_deleted=True, but does not clear references in trips or visited_countries. In contrast delete_photo :645-647 clears both cover_photo_id and photo_id references. enrich_trip :342-346 trusts an explicit cover_photo_id without checking is_deleted; serve_file :660 rejects the now-deleted photo.
item.expected: checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "Propagate ... delete ... changes to ... detail pages" and "Handle children on parent deletion". Deleting a city gallery should also invalidate its use as another entity's cover and choose a remaining image/fallback.
item.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: if a city's photograph is selected as the trip's cover, deleting that city soft-deletes the photo but leaves the trip pointing at it. The trip's card and hero permanently request a 404 image instead of choosing another surviving photo or a placeholder. The user can repair by selecting another cover; the broken images persist across reloads until then.
reproduction_steps: Create a trip with two cities and at least one photograph in each.
In Galería del viaje, choose a photo belonging to the first city as PORTADA.
Delete that city and its gallery.
Return to Mi perfil and the trip: its retained cover URL now answers 404 despite other photographs being available.
item.surface: Eliminar ciudad y su galería; trip card/hero covers
item.title: Deleting a city breaks the parent trip's cover image — cascade photo deletion leaves cover references intact

item.evidence: clerk_auth.py:115-116 verifies only JWT signature/claims locally; require_user :130-131 returns the token subject/session id without checking current session status. server.py:116-118 returns an existing profile without checking the provider user. No app logout/revocation endpoint or revocation store is present; AppShell.jsx:41,52 uses Clerk UserButton.
item.expected: checklist, Auth, sessions and access control: "the next-request rejection of revoked/deleted sessions" and "Sign-out ... ends a server-held session". A Clerk-revoked session must stop authorizing protected data/mutations, not just stop the browser issuing fresh tokens.
item.observed: Auth, sessions and access control: a copy of a still-unexpired session JWT continues authorizing app API reads and writes after its Clerk session is revoked or signed out, because the local verification path never consumes revocation state. Exposure is bounded by that JWT's expiry, whose configured duration is not available in source; indefinite access is not asserted. This weakens logout/revocation protection for users trying to end access to travel history.
reproduction_steps: Sign in and retain the current bearer token from an authorized app request.
Sign out/revoke that session in Mi cuenta.
Before the retained token's expiry, call a protected app route with it: the handler still trusts its signature and subject without checking revocation.
item.surface: Clerk sign-out/session revocation; all protected /api routes
item.title: Revoked sessions can still read or modify travel data until JWT expiry — backend never checks provider session revocation

item.evidence: Home.jsx:15 renders PageLoader whenever !data, including settled errors; Profile.jsx:19 and Stats.jsx:32 do the same. App.js:24 retries just once and disables refetchOnWindowFocus. Discover.jsx:41 and Cities.jsx:13 also treat missing failed data as loading. PhotoGallery.jsx:39 defaults missing failed data to [] and :90-93 labels it 'Aún no hay fotografías'.
item.expected: checklist, UI state, navigation and interaction: "Resolve initial, empty, pending, success, failure ... states" and "failure ending loading ... visible feedback and promised recovery". A rejected request must end loading, explain failure, and offer retry without falsely claiming there is no saved content.
item.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: on a network outage, backend 5xx or rejected session request, central pages remain a spinner indefinitely even after query retries finish; a failed gallery request instead claims there are no photographs. There is no visible error or retry action, and window focus does not refetch. Users cannot distinguish saved content loss from pending work and must reload/navigate to recover. These are source-predicted settled-error states.
reproduction_steps: Open Inicio or Mis estadísticas when its API read fails through both attempts.
Wait for retries to finish: the loading indicator remains with no error or retry.
Open an existing photographed city while only /photos fails: the gallery says Aún no hay fotografías.
item.surface: Inicio, Mi perfil, Mis estadísticas, Mis ciudades, Descubrir and photo galleries
item.title: Failed reads leave travelers stuck on spinners or false empty galleries — query errors are rendered as loading/empty states

item.evidence: Lightbox.jsx:9-12 handles ArrowRight/ArrowLeft globally without checking the event target; :14 attaches the handler to window. PhotoGallery.jsx:11 resets the editor draft whenever photo changes. PhotoEditor inputs at :21-23 are children of that lightbox, so normal caret/date arrow events bubble to the same listener.
item.expected: request: "Editar descripciones" and "Añadir fechas y ubicaciones"; checklist, Layout, theme, visuals and UX: "Follow shared event handling for keyboard ... use". Cursor and date navigation inside a field must edit that field, not switch the underlying photo and discard the draft.
item.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: while editing a caption/location or a date, pressing a left/right arrow changes the active photograph and resets the editor with another photo's values. The unsaved text disappears. This repeatedly disrupts normal keyboard editing, although users can retype and avoid arrow keys. Source prediction; no browser execution claimed.
reproduction_steps: Open a city gallery containing two photographs and click one image.
Type a new description without saving.
Press ArrowLeft to move the text cursor.
The lightbox switches images and the unsaved description is reset.
item.surface: Gallery fullscreen lightbox → photo description/date/location editor
item.title: Arrow-key editing discards photo descriptions — lightbox navigation intercepts keystrokes from its input fields

item.evidence: ProfileEditDialog.jsx:29-31 initializes the whole draft from me whenever [open, me] changes. onAvatar :39 immediately persists the avatar and :41 calls refresh(). useRefresh (lib/api.js:40) invalidates ['me']; the changed avatar causes a new me object and reinitializes all f fields, including unsaved bio/name/privacy values.
item.expected: request: "Edición del perfil"; checklist, UI state, navigation and interaction: "failed save preserving input" and settings/drafts reflect the current operation. Changing one profile field must not silently discard edits to other unsaved fields.
item.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: a traveler who writes a biography or changes privacy settings and then uploads an avatar loses those other pending edits as soon as /me refetch completes. The dialog stays open and announces only successful photo update, without warning about resetting the draft. A short draft can be re-entered; larger biography work is unnecessarily lost. Source-predicted race after the avatar request succeeds.
reproduction_steps: Open Editar perfil and type a new biography without Guardar perfil.
Upload a new profile photo using the avatar button.
Wait for Foto de perfil actualizada and the /me refresh.
The biography/privacy/name edits revert to the previous saved profile.
item.surface: Editar perfil → avatar upload while other fields are dirty
item.title: Uploading an avatar erases other pending profile edits — profile refetch reinitializes the entire open draft

item.evidence: search_cities :226-228 forwards all geocoder country_code values without mapping/filtering. create_city :475 calls check_country, whose :91-94 rejects codes absent from COUNTRY_BY_CODE. The reference list includes US (countries_data.py:181) but not PR; likewise FR exists but GP/MQ do not. CitySearch.jsx:38 selects those results unchanged and AddCityDialog.jsx:34 sends their code unchanged; non-manual selected countries cannot be changed (:77-81).
item.expected: request: "Buscador mundial de ciudades", "Las ciudades estarán vinculadas a su país correspondiente" and "193 miembros de Naciones Unidas y los dos Estados observadores". Inferred consistent contract: a valid territory city must map to its sovereign reference country without increasing the 195-country denominator; it must not be offered as a selectable but unsavable city.
item.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: when the world geocoder returns San Juan with PR (or other territory-specific ISO codes outside the reference list), the UI offers and selects it but saving always fails 'País no válido'. The selected result offers no country correction. Territory-city travelers cannot complete the promised worldwide-search registration through the normal flow; no provider response was executed, so the trigger is explicitly the geocoder returning its territory code.
reproduction_steps: Search worldwide for San Juan and choose the Puerto Rico result whose country_code is PR.
Fill visit dates and choose Guardar ciudad.
Whether marking the country too or saving only the city, backend validation rejects PR; the selected country's field is not editable.
item.surface: Añadir ciudad → worldwide CitySearch; POST /api/cities
item.title: Travelers cannot save offered territory cities — geocoder territory codes are incompatible with the 195-country validator

item.evidence: CitySearch.jsx:15 schedules a request; :19-20 sets its results unconditionally after completion; cleanup :24 only clears the debounce timer, never aborts an already started request or checks that q/country still match. :14 clears results for short input but cannot stop an older in-flight reply restoring them.
item.expected: request: "Buscarla. Seleccionarla." for worldwide city search; checklist, Business logic and calculations: "stale work must respect later decisions". Search results must belong to the current query/country, including when prior requests finish late.
item.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: if a previous search resolves after a newer one, its results overwrite the newer query's list. Clearing the input can also be undone by an old response, with obsolete city buttons reappearing. Travelers must re-enter the query and verify unfamiliar results instead of reliably selecting the requested destination. Scope is reordered network responses; no runtime latency was measured.
reproduction_steps: Type Roma and wait for its debounced request to start.
Change the search to Berlín and let that request finish first.
Let the earlier Roma request finish last; its results replace Berlín's results even though the input still says Berlín.
Alternatively clear the input before the first request returns; stale buttons can reappear.
item.surface: Worldwide city search in Añadir ciudad, Explorar and residence selection
item.title: City search shows results for an older query after users change it — in-flight requests have no cancellation or freshness guard

item.evidence: TripDetail.jsx:25 promises 'Las ciudades y fotos se conservarán sin viaje asignado.' server.py:401 deletes the trip and :403 sets its photos' trip_id=None. Photos uploaded directly to a trip have city_id=None (:589-605). PhotoGallery.jsx:35-39 can only request a city or trip gallery; App.js:33-36 has no standalone photo-library route. Home.jsx:88 routes an unlinked photo to '#', and server.py:701 caps recent images at 12.
item.expected: The app's deletion confirmation: "Las ciudades y fotos se conservarán sin viaje asignado"; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "Handle children on parent deletion by cascade, refusal or reassignment" and checklist, UI state, navigation and interaction: preserved work remains accessible. Keeping bytes but orphaning them from every usable gallery does not preserve their use for the owner.
item.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: deleting a trip with direct gallery uploads preserves records but removes their only navigable gallery. Unlinked photographs cannot be opened full-screen, edited, reassigned or deleted through the UI; only up to 12 recent thumbnails may appear on Inicio, pointing nowhere. Owners lose practical access to their photo history despite the explicit assurance; records can be recovered only through direct API/developer work or pre-retained file links, not the normal interface.
reproduction_steps: Create a trip with no cities and upload 20 photographs directly to Galería del viaje.
Choose Eliminar and accept the message promising photos will be preserved.
Return to Inicio/Mi perfil: the trip gallery is gone, there is no unassigned-photo library, and recent orphan thumbnails link to #.
Try to open or organize the preserved older photos through the UI; no destination exists.
item.surface: Eliminar viaje; Inicio recent photographs; absent unassigned photo library
item.title: Deleting a trip makes its direct photographs inaccessible despite a preservation promise — detached media has no gallery or reassignment flow

item.evidence: discover :791 returns only 60 profiles, without pagination or total. explore :800 first caps public profiles at 500, then :814-815 computes its ranking only over that subset; :817 labels len(public) as travelers. Explore.jsx:100 calls this 'perfiles públicos' and :112 links to 'Ver todos los perfiles', whose discover route remains capped.
item.expected: Explore.jsx:112: "Ver todos los perfiles"; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "pagination reaches the last page with counts under the same effective conditions ... exposes truncation"; checklist, Business logic and calculations: "a named leaderboard exposes the population it promises". All discoverable public travelers must be reachable, and ranking/count must use that same eligible population.
item.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: with 61 public profiles only 60 can be browsed in Descubrir and the UI provides no continuation; a traveler must know a missing person's name to search for them. At 501 public profiles, Explore reports only 500 and can omit the true highest-country traveler if they fall outside its unsorted first 500. This causes bounded missing discovery and incorrect community results rather than loss of private records.
reproduction_steps: With 61 eligible public profiles, open Explorar → Viajeros → Ver todos los perfiles.
Browse Descubrir: only 60 are returned and there is no page/load-more control.
With 501 profiles and the highest-country traveler outside the first 500 read by Explore, inspect the reported count and ranking: that traveler is excluded.
item.surface: Descubrir; Explorar → Ranking de viajeros and community count
item.title: Discover and community rankings omit eligible travelers — fixed unpaginated caps are presented as the full public population

item.evidence: server.py:810 groups distinct user ids into u; :812 uses {'$sort': {'u': -1}} and then $limit:24. MongoDB array sorting compares array element values, not length. Only after that limit does :813 sort the chosen subset by travelers=len(u). Explore.jsx:69-72 calls this 'Más visitadas por la comunidad'.
item.expected: Explore.jsx:69: "Más visitadas por la comunidad"; checklist, Business logic and calculations: "Establish ... numerator/denominator ... aggregation order". For this label, each city's popularity is the number of distinct eligible travelers; a city with 2 such travelers ranks ahead of every city with 1, regardless of their user-id ordering.
item.observed: Business logic and calculations: when more than 24 distinct cities exist, the database selects cities by lexicographic user-id values rather than traveler count. A two-traveler city can be discarded in favor of 24 single-traveler cities whose ids sort later; Python's later count-sort cannot restore the discarded popular city. The community is shown materially wrong recommendations for the stated popularity criterion. Source-predicted data ordering, not executed aggregation.
reproduction_steps: Have two eligible public travelers with lower-sorting ids record city A.
Have travelers with higher-sorting ids record 24 different cities, one eligible traveler each.
Open Explorar → Ciudades → Más visitadas por la comunidad.
City A can be missing because the limit was applied to user-id ordering before popularity sorting.
item.surface: GET /api/explore → top_cities; Explorar city popularity list
item.title: Popular cities are omitted in favor of less-visited ones — aggregation limits by user-id array ordering before counting travelers

item.evidence: PhotoGallery.jsx:63 updates items immediately, :64 posts the entire ordering, with no pending lock or serial queue. server.py:653-654 applies each ordering one photo at a time, unversioned. useRefresh at :65 can also trigger reads between overlapping writes.
item.expected: request: "Ordenar fotografías"; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "Walk plausible interleavings ... lost/overwritten valid work". For one user's successive reorder intents, the saved final order must reflect their latest completed sequence, not a delayed earlier request.
item.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: users can make two reorder moves quickly while the first request is pending. If the earlier request reaches the server last, it overwrites the later full order; interleaved loops can also create tied order values. Reload restores the wrong sequence even though the UI showed the final move. Recovery is manual reordering, so the impairment is bounded but repeatedly undermines the requested organizer.
reproduction_steps: With photos A,B,C, enable Ordenar and move A right once, then right again before the first save finishes.
Let the request for the first order [B,A,C] complete after the second [B,C,A].
Reload the city gallery: the stored order can revert to the earlier intent rather than keeping [B,C,A].
item.surface: City Galería → Ordenar; POST /api/photos/reorder
item.title: Quick photo moves revert after reload — overlapping reorder saves can overwrite the user's latest order

item.evidence: share_trip :410 and share_city :545 always reuse any existing share_token; their only mutation is setting that token. Public access :751 and :761 checks only token equality. TripUpdate/CityUpdate schemas have no revocation setting and there is no revoke/rotate share route. The corresponding UI exposes only Compartir/Compartir galería, editing and whole-record deletion; profile privacy is not consulted by these shared handlers.
item.expected: request: "Cada usuario podrá decidir qué información quiere compartir" and "Compartir viajes individualmente"; checklist, Auth, sessions and access control: "Follow ... expired grants ... through every supported access path". Inferred privacy table stake: an owner can stop a previously authorized share without destroying their own travel record and gallery.
item.observed: Auth, sessions and access control: after sharing a city or trip, the owner cannot withdraw access from old recipients or a forwarded link. Making the profile private, hiding photos, or disabling the trip's public-profile switch does not stop that token. Pressing Compartir again redistributes the same grant. The only available revocation is deleting the entire city/trip, which destroys the record/gallery access and is not a safe privacy control. This is a missing revocation capability proven by the complete route/control inventory, not a claim that any specific recipient accessed the link.
reproduction_steps: Share a city or trip and open the link in another browser.
Attempt to stop sharing while retaining the travel record: inspect Editar, profile privacy and Compartir.
Make the profile private and disable public-trip visibility, then reopen the old share URL.
It continues to return the shared content; no revoke or new-link action is available.
item.surface: Compartir viaje / Compartir galería; shared links and privacy controls
item.title: Owners cannot stop sharing a city or trip without deleting it — permanent share tokens have no revoke or rotation path

item.evidence: Lightbox.jsx:19 renders a fixed ordinary div, with no dialog role, focus ref, focus initialization, modal primitive, inert background or focus trap. Its only effect (:8-16) is a global keydown listener. By contrast the shared dialog component (components/ui/dialog.jsx:26-43) uses Radix's modal Content, but Lightbox does not use it. Gallery thumbnails and app navigation remain mounted before the lightbox in the DOM.
item.expected: checklist, Layout, theme, visuals and UX: "keyboard focus ... follows the active surface" and "an editor overlay must preserve the supported focus/background interaction contract". Opening a fullscreen photo editor must move keyboard focus into that editor and keep Tab navigation within its visible controls until closing.
item.observed: Layout, theme, visuals and UX: opening a photo leaves focus on the now-covered background thumbnail. Tab continues through other hidden gallery/app controls before reaching the overlay, and can later leave it again. On a 200-photo gallery, keyboard travelers may need to traverse most hidden thumbnails to reach the caption/date controls, or can accidentally activate background navigation and dismiss their work. Escape/arrow browsing is present, but it does not make editing controls readily reachable. This is a source-backed focus prediction, not a measured layout claim.
reproduction_steps: Using only the keyboard, open the first image in a large city gallery.
Press Tab to reach the fullscreen photo-editor controls.
Focus remains in the background gallery rather than entering/staying within the overlay; hidden controls can be activated.
item.surface: Fullscreen gallery lightbox/photo editor
item.title: Keyboard users tab through hidden background controls instead of the photo editor — fullscreen overlay never takes or traps focus

item.evidence: startup :886 launches ensure_indexes as a background task and never awaits it before accepting traffic. ensure_indexes :70 builds unique indexes and :71-72 merely logs failures. get_profile :116 checks then :132 inserts a new random profile; no atomic upsert is used. Unique user_id/id/username constraints exist only in the index list (:42-46).
item.expected: R-002: "creates a user with a stable unique id and one profile owned by that id" and "duplicate registration must be refused by the store, not only by the form"; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "A check before insert alone races". Before provisioning is available, profile uniqueness must already be enforced and failed constraint initialization must not leave the app serving unconstrained writes.
item.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: on a fresh database when index building is slower than startup's storage initialization, two first requests for the same authenticated user can both see no profile and insert separate profiles before the unique user_id index exists. Subsequent index creation then fails on those duplicates and is only logged, leaving both profiles and no constraint. Different stable profile ids can be returned for the same traveler and social references can attach to whichever record a read selects. Scope is first-start/index-failure timing; no claim is made that existing correctly indexed databases reproduce it.
reproduction_steps: Start the supplied app against a fresh database under conditions where creating indexes is still pending when startup returns.
Register a user and issue concurrent first /api/me and /api/home requests for that same authenticated identity.
Both profile lookups can precede either insertion while the unique user_id constraint is absent.
Observe from the source sequence that two random profile records can commit and the later unique-index failure is logged instead of blocking service.
item.surface: Fresh deployment startup; lazy profile creation on first authenticated requests
item.title: One newly registered traveler can receive duplicate profiles during startup — unique-index creation runs after writes become available

item.evidence: AddCityDialog.jsx:41 POSTs city before :42 uploads files; failure goes to :47 with no refresh or retained city id. TripDialog.jsx:32 creates trip before :34 uploads cover, with the same catch at :41. AddCountryDialog.jsx:33 creates visited country before :35 uploads photo; catch :42 leaves creation mode, while server.py:275-276 rejects the now-existing country. For a gallery batch, server.py:604-605 commits each file individually via store_upload (:580-584) before validating later files; PhotoGallery.jsx:51-56 reports a generic error with no successful-subset refresh/reconciliation if a later file fails.
item.expected: checklist, UI state, navigation and interaction: "Read ... every durable/external effect and visible result together" and "a failed save preserving input"; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "Multi-document operations leave no half-written state on failure"; checklist, Files, media and generated artifacts: "visible rejected/skipped input". A retry must continue the same saved intent or clearly expose the partial result and successful subset.
item.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: if upload fails (provider outage, oversized file, interrupted request), the earlier entity is already durable but the dialog reports failure and remains open without refreshing lists. Retrying Guardar ciudad or Crear viaje creates another entity, and retrying a country returns 'Ya tienes este país registrado' instead of finishing its photo. In a gallery batch containing a valid image followed by an oversized file, the valid image is already stored but the UI reports only failure; retrying the batch duplicates the successful prefix. Users must close/reload, identify partially saved work and repair it manually, with duplicate visits also corrupting counts. Source-predicted failure sequences; no runtime calls made.
reproduction_steps: Create a city with a photograph larger than 25 MiB (or during a storage outage).
Press Guardar ciudad and, if prompted, Solo la ciudad.
After the error, press Guardar ciudad again.
Close the dialog and reload Mis ciudades: the city was created on both attempts. Repeat the country flow to see the duplicate-country rejection instead.

In an existing gallery, upload one valid JPEG followed by an oversized image. After failure, retry the same selection and then reload: the valid prefix has been saved twice, without any partial-success explanation.
item.surface: Añadir ciudad; Nuevo viaje with cover; Añadir país visitado with photo; multi-file gallery uploads
item.title: Failed uploads leave hidden partial work and retries create duplicates or get stuck — writes commit before the whole save/upload succeeds
